title: Choose the visual world for MyThaiTaxes
question: The roll assigned Carbon-Copy Form Set. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Carbon-Copy Form Set
options.lineage: Thai office paperwork: boxed-digit forms, carbonless triplicate copies, rubber stamps
options.thesis: The home page is a fanned stack of coloured carbon-copy sheets, one per calculator, and the top sheet is a live form you fill in.
materials: carbonless copy paper in white, canary, pink and blue
ultramarine form ruling and boxed digit cells
options.viewport: Full-height ultramarine desk; four fanned sheets tabbed Quick / Annual / Monthly / Foreign income; the white top sheet takes income into boxed digits and stamps the tax due live; a perforated 'tear here' tab is the scroll arrow.
options.risk: Paperwork can read bureaucratic if the colours are timid; it must look like a joyful stack, not a government form, and never imitate an official Revenue Department form.

raised.raise: Every figure wears a provenance ticket: its source and tax year printed beside it, like a stall tag.
The working form always sits on the nearest sheet; nothing decorative ever covers an input.
One strict state vocabulary: filled box = entered, struck line = not applicable, stamp = result.
The monthly sheet's 12-month withholding row is one unbroken line that scales, never wraps.
Each sheet's tab edge is its summary; pulling it forward is the detail.
Stamp red is reserved for the live result and nothing else.

options.label: Skytrain Line Map
options.lineage: Bangkok rail wayfinding: coloured lines, station roundels, platform signs
options.thesis: Your tax situation is a journey: each calculator is a coloured line and each step a station.
options.viewport: A line map across the hero: four coloured lines branch from 'Your income', the quick estimate is the first station with a live fare-style result.
options.risk: Transit-map sites are a familiar design trope; it is the direction most runs would reach for.

options.label: Moon-Shadow Bazaar
options.thesis: Tax figures traded as goods at moonlit stalls.
options.viewport: A night lane of stalls, one per calculator.
options.case: Night markets are familiar to expats, but surreal shadow trade blurs a number people must trust.

options.label: Multiplane Cel Dawn
options.thesis: Scroll as a camera sinking through painted layers.
options.viewport: Painted forest planes with the calculator on the nearest cel.
options.case: No connection to Thai tax for foreigners; heavy painted assets we cannot produce here.
options.kept: Interactive layer always on the nearest plane.

options.label: One-Bit Desktop
options.thesis: Calculators as overlapping windows on a dithered desktop.
options.case: Directly opposes the ask for more colour.

options.label: Rhythm Step Row
options.thesis: Twelve months as a step row with a chase light.
options.viewport: 12 lit month keys with tax per month.
options.case: Clever for withholding, but expats do not see themselves in a drum machine.
options.kept: The 12-month row as one unbroken line.

options.label: Window-Box Toy Shelf
options.thesis: Each calculator as a boxed set on a shelf.
options.viewport: A shelf of calculator boxes, lids that open.
options.case: Playful in a way that undercuts trust in a tax number.
options.kept: Front is summary, opening is detail.

options.label: Polish Film Poster
options.thesis: One painted metaphor swallowing the page.
options.viewport: A painted metaphor of tax with lettering on its contours.
options.case: Hides the calculator; needs painted art we cannot generate.
options.kept: Hottest red reserved for the one thing in focus.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean fintech calculator landing page, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Split hero: headline and promise left, a calculator card with tabs for each tool right, trust row under it.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other tax calculator by design.
